title: Box Breathing
description: Equal-duration breathing in four gentle counts to restore calm and balance your nervous system.
steps: Gently exhale all air from your lungs.
Breathe in slowly through your nose for 4 counts.
Hold your breath gently for 4 counts without straining.
Slowly exhale through your mouth for 4 counts.
Hold empty for 4 counts, then repeat softly.

title: 4-7-8 Breathing
description: An extended exhale practice that signals safety to your body and helps quiet a racing mind.
steps: Settle into a comfortable, relaxed posture.
Inhale quietly through your nose for a count of 4.
Gently hold your breath for a count of 7.
Exhale completely and audibly through your mouth for a count of 8.
Repeat this gentle cycle 3 to 4 times.

title: Physiological Sigh
description: A double inhale followed by a long, relaxed sigh to rapidly reset tension.
steps: Take a deep, full breath in through your nose.
At the very top, take a second quick sharp inhale to fully fill your lungs.
Release with a long, slow, vocalized or soft sigh through your mouth.
Repeat 2 to 3 times whenever you feel immediate tightness.

title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
description: Gently anchor your awareness in your immediate surroundings using your physical senses.
steps: Acknowledge 5 things you can see around you right now.
Notice 4 things you can physically touch or feel (like your clothes or the chair).
Listen for 3 distinct sounds in your environment.
Notice 2 things you can smell (or two scents you enjoy).
Notice 1 thing you can taste or take a mindful sip of water.

title: Body Scan
description: A gentle check-in from head to toe to notice and soften areas holding unnoticed tension.
steps: Rest your feet flat and let your hands soften in your lap.
Bring gentle attention to your face and jaw; let your teeth separate slightly.
Drop your shoulders away from your ears and let your chest soften.
Notice your stomach, hips, and legs, inviting each part to relax.
Take one deep breath appreciating your body just as it is right now.

title: Release & Unclench
description: Intentionally notice and relax the common spots where everyday stress quietly gathers.
steps: Notice if your tongue is pressed to the roof of your mouth; let it drop.
Check your forehead and eyebrows; smooth them out.
Unclench your hands and let your fingers curl naturally.
Release your stomach muscles and take a gentle, unrestricted breath.
Enjoy the subtle feeling of space and lightness.

title: Brain Dump
description: Empty your mental clutter onto the page without worrying about neatness, order, or grammar.
steps: Open a blank space or paper.
Write down everything swirling in your mind: tasks, worries, random thoughts.
Keep typing or writing continuously for two minutes without editing.
Acknowledge that your thoughts are now safe outside of your head.

title: One Small Next Step
description: When everything feels big, narrow your focus down to just one tiny, manageable action.
steps: Think about what is currently feeling heavy or stuck.
Ask yourself: 'What is the absolute smallest next step I can take in under 5 minutes?'
Write that single micro-step down clearly.
Give yourself permission to ignore everything else until that one step is done.

title: Gratitude Moment
description: Shift your focus to a small comfort, kindness, or steady presence in your day.
steps: Think of 2 or 3 tiny things that brought a moment of ease today (e.g., warm tea, fresh air, a kind word).
Write them down and note why each felt pleasant.
Pause for 30 seconds to genuinely savor the warmth of those moments.

title: Name What You Feel
description: Give compassionate language to your current emotional state to reduce its intensity.
steps: Take a slow breath and ask yourself with kindness: 'What am I feeling right now?'
Put words to the emotion without judging yourself for having it.
Write a short supportive sentence, such as: 'It is understandable that I feel this way right now.'
Offer yourself patience as you navigate this moment.

title: Screen/Movement Break
description: Step away from your display, stretch your limbs, and give your eyes and mind a physical change of scenery.
steps: Push back your chair and step away from all screens.
Look out a window or gaze at something at least 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Roll your shoulders backward 5 times and gently stretch your arms overhead.
Walk a short loop around your room or drink a glass of fresh water.
Return feeling slightly recharged and refreshed.

title: Break It Into One Small Step
description: When an assignment, study goal, or work project feels massive, slice it down to a single 2-minute starter action.
steps: Write down the specific academic or work task that feels daunting right now.
Ask yourself: 'What is the absolute smallest physical action I can take in under two minutes?' (e.g. open the document, read one paragraph).
Commit to doing just that one micro-step without worrying about finishing the whole project.
Acknowledge that starting is the hardest part, and one step creates forward momentum.

title: 25-Minute Focus Sprint
description: A structured, distraction-free focus interval to help you make tangible progress on your study or work task.
steps: Choose one clear assignment or work task to focus on exclusively.
Silence all non-essential phone and browser notifications.
Work steadily with gentle focus for 25 minutes until the timer concludes.
When finished, step away from your desk for a well-deserved 5-minute pause.

title: Name the Worry, Then Park It
description: A structured 5-minute worry time-box: acknowledge what is troubling you, write it down, and consciously park it for later.
steps: Set a mental boundary: you have 5 minutes to acknowledge your worries without judging them.
Write down the specific worry currently taking up mental bandwidth.
Categorize it: is this something you have control over right now, or is it out of your hands?
If within control, write one future action step; if outside your control, draw a box around it to 'park' it for today.
Take one deep breath and transition your focus back to the present moment.

title: Reach Out to One Person
description: A simple, low-pressure prompt to send one supportive text or check-in message to someone in your life.
steps: Think of one friend, family member, classmate, or colleague you feel comfortable with.
Draft a short, zero-pressure message (e.g. 'Thinking of you, hope your day is going well!' or a friendly emoji).
Hit send without waiting anxiously for an immediate response.
Notice the subtle shift that comes from extending a small connection outward.

title: Sleep Wind-Down
description: A progressive slowing breath pattern and body relaxing ritual designed to prepare your mind for restful sleep.
steps: Dim your lights and settle into a comfortable lying or reclining position.
Place one hand on your stomach and breathe in slowly for 4 counts, feeling your belly gently rise.
Exhale smoothly through your mouth for 6 counts, allowing your shoulders and jaw to sink into the bed.
Notice any lingering thoughts from the day and visualize setting them aside on a bedside table until tomorrow.
Continue this gentle rhythm until your breathing feels natural, heavy, and calm.

title: Self-Kindness Pause
description: A gentle reframing exercise (practical wellbeing reflection, explicitly not therapy) to replace harsh self-criticism with supportive patience.
steps: Notice if your internal voice has been harsh, frustrated, or demanding today.
Ask yourself: 'What would a patient, supportive friend say to me right now about this situation?'
Write down that kinder perspective in one or two clear sentences.
Remind yourself that doing your best with today's energy is entirely enough.

title: Small Comfort Act
description: Do one small, nurturing physical thing to bring a tiny spark of warmth or relief to your space.
steps: Ask yourself: 'What is one tiny physical comfort I could give myself right now?' (e.g. wrap in a blanket, warm tea, splash face).
Spend two minutes preparing or doing that one small comforting act.
Pause for a moment and allow yourself to receive that comfort without guilt.
Take one deep breath and acknowledge that you deserve kindness today.

title: Savour the Moment
description: Notice what is feeling steady or pleasant right now and intentionally prolong that positive feeling.
steps: Identify one pleasant or neutral physical sensation right now (e.g. comfortable seat, warm drink, steady breath).
Direct your full, unhurried attention toward this sensation for 60 seconds.
Notice how your mind and body respond when you intentionally savor ease.
Anchor this feeling with a gentle, appreciative breath.

title: Set One Intention
description: Anchor your calm or steady energy by choosing one mindful, purposeful intention for the hours ahead.
steps: Reflect on how you want to carry yourself through the rest of the day.
Choose a single anchor word or intention (e.g., 'patience', 'focus', 'gentleness', 'boundaries').
Write down that one word and one way you will embody it today.
Keep this intention quietly in mind as you resume your activities.

title: Brain Dump + Pick One
description: When multiple tasks compete for attention, list them all rapidly and choose exactly one to address.
steps: Rapidly list every task, email, or worry currently cluttering your head without editing.
Read through the list once and draw a circle around the single highest-leverage item.
Give yourself explicit permission to ignore every other item on the page for now.
Take a deep breath knowing that tackling one priority is the antidote to paralysis.

title: Shoulder Release Stretch
description: Release physical tightness accumulated in your neck, shoulders, and upper back from daily stress.
steps: Sit upright and gently shrug your shoulders up to your ears on an inhale.
Hold for 3 seconds, then exhale and drop your shoulders completely.
Roll your shoulders backwards in slow, wide circles 5 times.
Gently tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder for 15 seconds, then repeat on the left.
Notice the newfound sense of space and release around your neck.

title: Name One Good Thing
description: Take sixty seconds to name one small thing that is good, comfortable, or comforting right now.
steps: Pause and look around or scan your memory for one tiny positive detail.
Name it softly or write it down on paper.
Let the simple goodness of that one thing sink in for thirty seconds.

title: Stand and Stretch 60 Seconds
description: Stand up, raise your arms high, and take a long stretch to wake up your body and clear physical fatigue.
steps: Stand up tall away from your seat.
Interlace your fingers and reach gently toward the ceiling.
Take one deep inhale, exhale, roll your shoulders down, and sit back down feeling slightly taller.

title: Music Reset
description: Play one uplifting or soothing song to shift your energy and reset your emotional state.
steps: Put on headphones or turn on a favorite, comforting track.
Close your eyes and listen purely to the rhythm and melody for two minutes.
Notice how your heartbeat and energy shift with the music.

title: Message One Friend
description: Send a quick, low-effort emoji or hello to one friend to feel connected and less isolated.
steps: Pick one person you feel comfortable with.
Send a short greeting, funny meme, or warm emoji without expecting an instant reply.
Enjoy the warm spark of reaching outward.

title: Splash and Reset
description: Splash cool water on your face or wrists to activate your dive reflex and quickly calm physical agitation.
steps: Walk to the sink and run cool tap water over your wrists.
Gently splash cool water onto your face and temples.
Pat dry with a soft towel and take one clear, fresh breath.

title: Pick the One Thing That Matters
description: When everything feels demanding, identify the single thing that truly matters today.
steps: Look at everything currently on your mind.
Ask yourself: If I could only finish one thing today, which would give me the most peace?
Circle that one task and set everything else aside for tomorrow.

title: Write It Down, Then Park It
description: Put swirling thoughts and worries onto paper, draw a box around them, and park them for later.
steps: Write down the specific thoughts spinning in your mind without censoring yourself.
Draw a neat box around the list to contain it on the page.
Tell yourself: This is recorded safely; I do not need to hold it in my head right now.

title: Decide the Next 20 Minutes
description: Narrow your focus to only the next twenty minutes to break through mental freeze.
steps: Ignore the rest of the day and ask: What is one simple thing I can do in the next 20 minutes?
Write down that single step (e.g. read one section, clear one drawer).
Set a 20-minute timer and begin gently without rushing.

title: Write the Unsent Message
description: Vent in writing without sending it, allowing your emotions to clear before deciding how to respond.
steps: Open a private, offline blank note or grab a piece of paper.
Write out everything you are feeling, thinking, and wishing you could say without filtering.
Review what you wrote and remind yourself this is private venting, not something to send.
If this involves unfair workloads or conflict, remember talking to a supervisor or teacher is also an option.

title: List Who Owns What
description: Map out all shared deliverables, who owns each item, and clearly highlight unowned tasks.
steps: List all deliverables or sections required for this project or goal.
Assign names beside each item based on what was agreed upon.
Highlight any unassigned tasks in a separate column so gaps are factual and visible.
If teammates remain unresponsive, sharing this neutral list with an instructor or manager is a healthy option.

title: Draft One Clear Ask
description: Draft one specific, respectful request with a clear deadline using the format I need X by Y.
steps: Identify the single deliverable you need from the other person right now.
Draft a clear, polite sentence: I need [specific task] completed by [day and time] so we can submit on time.
Read it over to ensure the tone is factual and constructive rather than confrontational.
Keep in mind that if collaboration breaks down, seeking guidance from a teacher or lead is also an option.

title: Pick Your Conversation Moment
description: Choose an unhurried time and calm setting for a sensitive conversation, plus one neutral opening sentence.
steps: Choose a time when neither of you is in a rush or already exhausted.
Decide whether a quick private voice call, in-person chat, or calm note is best.
Write down one neutral opening sentence (e.g. I want to make sure we are on the same page about our deadline.).
Remember you can always invite a neutral supervisor, teacher, or trusted third party to facilitate.

title: Separate Facts from Feelings
description: Create two columns to distinguish the observable facts of what happened from the emotions and stories around it.
steps: Draw a line down the center of a page: label the left Observable Facts and the right How I Felt.
On the left, write only verifiable events (e.g. No message received by 3 PM).
On the right, acknowledge your emotional reactions (e.g. Felt dismissed and anxious).
Notice how seeing the objective facts frees up mental clarity to address the situation constructively.

title: Plan B for the Deadline
description: Define the minimum viable submission you can produce independently if help does not arrive on time.
steps: Identify the core requirements needed to submit a passing, valid draft of the project.
Outline what you can realistically complete on your own before the cutoff time.
Prepare a short, factual note to your teacher or supervisor explaining what portion you completed.
Acknowledge that taking proactive control protects your standing and eases last-minute panic.
